text: Case study: a retail inventory data platform — where two genuinely different computations justify Lambda architecture's extra cost.

A restock trigger needs a simple running total per SKU per store, under five minutes stale. Nightly merchandising needs full reconciliation against shipments, returns, and shrinkage — a materially different computation, not the same logic replayed.

Speed layer keeps a running on-hand total for the trigger. Batch layer reconciles everything overnight for merchandising. This is the honest counter-example to Kappa: not every platform reduces to one replayable codepath.

Corporate merchandising needs to roll up inventory across every store, which rules out siloed tenancy. One fact table, FactInventoryMovement, feeds a near-real-time rollup for the trigger and a nightly reconciled view for reports — same shape, two SLAs.
The schema doesn't change between consumers — only which materialized view of it they read. Next up: a social media analytics pipeline.
